open.why: it offers ES256, ES384, ES512 — three ECDSA curves and no Ed25519. `fido2-token -I` prints the third as `unknown`, which is libfido2 not naming COSE -36; asking the device for the numbers is what turns a guess into a ruling

aaguid_note: An AAGUID is sixteen bytes a firmware asserts about itself, identical on every board that flashes the same image. Claiming one is code — which is why this is not a counterexample to exp176 calling the difference certification. What exp176 named was the authority behind it and the secret it has to be kept with, and neither is a thing a firmware can assert about itself. Without Secure Lock, which this road does not burn, exp175 applies to this image exactly as it applied to ours.
